# forkalope

> forkalope is hands-on SRE and DevOps training. Students learn on real systems, prove their production judgment through observed work, and can qualify as Forkalope Operators before joining a trusted operator network.

## Start here

- [Forkalope flight school](https://forkalope.com/): Read how the program, curriculum, checkride, pricing principle, and graduate operator network are being designed.
- [The landscape](https://forkalope.com/landscape/): Research into open-source Git forges and the design space for a shared cloud of independently operated nodes.
- [FAQ](https://forkalope.com/faq/): Answers about the forge, shared recovery, Co-Sysops, and business hosting.
- [Co-Sysops](https://forkalope.com/co-sysops/): Learn how to help fund or operate the shared cloud.
- [For business](https://forkalope.com/business/): Hosting options for businesses, including managed, dedicated, and customer infrastructure.
- [Partners](https://forkalope.com/partners/): Partner programs for migrations, support, infrastructure operation, and related work.

## Flight school

- The school is the first product. The open-source Forkalope forge is the training aircraft.
- SRE is the external career category; DevOps is useful adjacent language. “Forkalope Operator” is the internal qualification and identity.
- The program is designed around ground school, failure simulators, supervised operating hours, and a final checkride.
- Graduates leave with inspectable evidence: runbooks, incident reports, reviewed changes, drill history, and checkride results.
- Qualified graduates may later contribute to the forge, mentor students, join the operator network, or apply for paid work. None of those outcomes is guaranteed by tuition.
- The first cohort is still being designed. Paid enrollment is not open yet.

## Policies

- [Privacy](https://forkalope.com/privacy/): Draft privacy policy for the website, repositories, and network of independent operators.
- [Terms](https://forkalope.com/terms/): Starter terms for Co-Sysop memberships, node operators, managed hosting, and related work.

## Source

- [Forkalope web repository](https://github.com/forkalope/web): Public source for the website and current forge build.
